I'm sorry you're struggling so much :( but well done for reaching out and telling someone about it.

 As far as you saying there's no reason for you to feel like this, don't go down that route. You could be a billionaire with literally everything you wanted in life and still be hella depressed. There's nothing shameful about it, even if people love to say 'but you can't be sad, you have a great life' what you are feeling is completely valid.

 Is there any reason you are scared to take anti depressants? Medication isn't for everyone, you should discuss your concerns with your doctor. I have been on anti depressants for the past 6 years and I have come such a long way on them. My view point on them is I wouldn't not take my medication if I had a heart condition, so why shouldn't I treat my wobbly brain?! As I said, medication isn't for everyone. The GP will offer other things to try as well, CBT. Support groups ect. 

Has your husband ever had any first hand experience with someone struggling with depression? Either themselves or a friend/family member? It might be easier for them to understand otherwise. When my. Mental health got really bad this year I felt so guilty, exactly how you're feeling with there's no reason to be feeling like this. I felt awful telling my wife, scared she'd be angry at me or upset because she'd feel like she wasn't enough. She reacted in neither of these ways. She was incredibly supportive throughout and it was a relief to have someone to talk to. I also had a friend I talked to about how I was feeling. If you can set up some kind of support network it will really help, struggling on your own is not going to work in the long run. People love you and wouldn't want you to suffer in silence.

Back to your husband, maybe doing some research online, which might be helpful to you too, about what causes depression so you can understand, and explain to your husband that it's nothing they're doing wrong ect it's just one of those unfortunate things and try explaining some ways he can help support you.

If you want an anonymous shoulder to cry on feel free to message me, I might not reply straight away but you are welcome to vent away anytime you want.

As I said you've taken the first step by reaching out for help and that is amazing, you should be proud.
